root_cause_label: Agent assumed /opt/miniswea/bin/python3 was the system-wide interpreter and installed/patched fasttext there; the benchmark tests run under /usr/local Python where the fix was never applied.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly diagnosed the NumPy 2.x copy=False incompatibility and applied the right patch, but did so inside the /opt/miniswea virtual environment rather than the /usr/local system Python used by the benchmark tests, so the fix never reached the tested installation.
t_err_evidence: Step 3 installs fasttext into /opt/miniswea/lib/python3.13/site-packages/ using /opt/miniswea/bin/python3 pip, acting on the false premise that /opt/miniswea/bin/python3 is the 'default system-wide Python interpreter' rather than targeting /usr/local.
t_commit_evidence: Once fasttext is installed exclusively in /opt/miniswea in step 3, all subsequent work (diagnosis in step 4, source location in step 5, patching in step 6) operates on that wrong installation; no later step switches to /usr/local, locking in the failure.
t_surface_evidence: Step 4 terminal output shows 'Predict failed: Unable to avoid copy while creating an array as requested' — the first observable failure signal (though it is the secondary NumPy bug, not the primary env mismatch).
trigger_explanation: Step 2 clearly shows 'Executable: /opt/miniswea/bin/python3', indicating this is a virtual/managed environment rather than the system interpreter. The agent's step 3 analysis states it is acting on the 'default system-wide Python interpreter' — an unverified and incorrect assumption. The agent never checked /usr/local/bin/python3 or verified which interpreter the benchmark tests actually use.
forewarning_evidence: Step 2 terminal output explicitly shows 'Executable: /opt/miniswea/bin/python3', which is a non-system-wide path that should have prompted verification of which interpreter pytest/the benchmark uses; instead the agent proceeded to install into this environment without checking.
